title: POC Weekly - Onboard & Ops Gateway Readiness
summary: Weekly POC sync to review this week's benchmark runs and infra readiness. Main items: minor p99 tail latency regression on long prompts, gateway auth token expiry issue, need to finalize KMS integration and SSO, and decide on a short dedicated capacity pilot for peak traffic days. Next steps include issuing security pack, scheduling a focused latency run with synthetic traffic, and Samir to coordinate staging creds with Dana.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-26
Start: 09:30 PT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM), Michael Ortiz (Nexara CTO), Leila Kim (Platform Eng), Omar Haddad (Security Lead), Dana Rivas (SRE), Priya Shah (PM)

Summary: quick bench recap, infra gating items, security/KMS/SSO checklist, next steps and owners.

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining on time, appreciate it. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Michael (Nexara): Michael here.
[00:08] Leila (Nexara): Leila.
[00:09] Omar (Nexara): Omar.
[00:10] Dana (Nexara): Dana.
[00:11] Jordan: great, Samir and Priya from our side as well. super quick agenda - bench results, any infra blockers, security items, and then actions. Sound ok?
[00:20] Michael: yes that works. we had the team review the runs you sent last night. thanks for those.
[00:25] Jordan: cool. Priya, do you want to run through the numbers?
[00:28] Priya (Redwood SE): yeah sure. so we ran three runs against the staging gateway with the workload profile you gave us. run A was baseline with no caching, run B enabled prefix/KV cache, run C simulated a mixed traffic pattern with 25% long prompts - about 2k tokens average for the long subset. aggregate p50s are fine - ~85ms token step for small, and p95 sitting around 180ms, but we saw p99 spikes up to ~1.1s on long prompts in run C. there is also a small bump in cold-starts when the kv cache miss rate is high.
[01:10] Leila: thanks. is that 1.1 seconds per token or per response? i think there was some confusion in the sheet.
[01:16] Priya: good call - that's end-to-end inference tail for the request, not per token. so a full response taking 1.1s sometimes. most responses are 200-400ms.
[01:25] Dana: from infra we saw that gateway CPU was peaking during those bursts; some of the auth validation loops are doing synchronous calls to our user directory which added latency under burst.
[01:37] Omar: yep that ties to our token expiry config. we noticed the bearer token refresh hits Keycloak for every new session currently. we should batch or cache it.
[01:45] Samir (Redwood CSM): ok that sounds like a combined app-side issue + KV cache tuning. Priya, can Redwood replicate the auth token churn locally to prove model-side isn't the root cause?
[01:55] Priya: yes, we can inject token refresh calls in the synthetic runs; that'll show how much of the 1.1s is infra vs model. I'll add that for the next sweep.
[02:05] Jordan: also worth noting we ran a quantized variant in run B (4-bit q) and cost per token dropped ~30% with minimal quality delta on your eval set. but latency profile changed slightly - fewer GPU kernel warmups but higher per-batch variance.
[02:22] Michael: curious - for production we'd rather assume predictable latency over slight cost savings, so what's the knob to favor stability?
[02:29] Priya: two levers: dedicated capacity with pinned instances, and tighter batch sizing + pre-warm. batch size limits and target latency SLOs can be set in the rollout policy. dedicated will reduce eviction and kernel warmups.
[02:42] Leila: can you remind us the minimum commit for dedicated? we need rough pricing to take to procurement.
[02:47] Jordan: i'll send a pricing note — short answer: we can provision a small reserved pool for two weeks as a pilot; i'll propose options in the follow up.
[02:55] Michael: great.
[02:57] [03:00] Priya: back to the bench: with KV cache on, p99 improved substantially for short prompts but only marginally for long ones. long prompts benefit from prefix caching only if the prompt prefix repeats frequently. your current long prompt set is fairly unique per user so cache hit rate stayed low.
[03:20] Dana: right our clinical note expansions are pretty free-form, not repeated. any other caching options?
[03:25] Priya: yes, we can enable partial KV reuse — e.g., cache recent token windows for same user session — it's more complicated but can help. it also depends on session affinity at the gateway.
[03:36] Omar: security wise, KMS integration question — we support HashiCorp Vault and AWS KMS. which do you need for key wrapping?
[03:43] Jordan: we support both. if you want HSM-backed keys we can integrate with your vendor; we just need the access patterns.
[03:50] Omar: perfect, i'll send the KMS decision and expected envelope key rotation cadence.
[03:56] Leila: there was a gateway error we saw yesterday when we hit 2k concurrent, some 502s surfaced. did you see the same?
[04:03] Priya: yes, 502s were correlated with connection pool exhaustion on the gateway side. we bumped pool sizes in the staging run and the 502 rate dropped. however, we need your team to confirm NAT and firewall connection tracking settings -they were dropping idle connections after 60s which caused reconnect storms.
[04:20] Dana: noted, we'll check conntracking and idle timeouts.
[04:23] [04:30] Jordan: quick question on observability - do you need token-level cost breakdown or just per-route?
[04:30] Priya Shah (Nexara PM): per-route is fine initially, token-level will be helpful later.
[04:36] Jordan: ok we'll include per-route in the next dashboard export.
[04:40] Michael: one more ask on compliance - can you provide audit logs for inference requests? we need that for our SOC2 threshold.
[04:45] Samir: yes, audit logs are available and we can forward logs to your SIEM; we'll include retention policy options in the security pack.
[04:52] Omar: also SSO — we use SAML with Okta, and we want RBAC mapped to roles in the console. is that supported?
[04:59] Jordan: yes SAML+Okta is supported, RBAC role mapping is configurable. Samir will help with the mapping.
[05:05] Samir: noted. i'll draft a mapping template and share.
[05:09] [05:15] Priya: for the next technical run i'd like to isolate variables: 1) token churn only, 2) cache disabled, 3) cache enabled partial, 4) dedicated instances pre-warmed. that'll let us attribute p99 causes.
[05:27] Leila: sounds good. is there a way to reproduce the long prompts with the same distribution? we can seed some synthetic but it's hard to match clinical variety.
[05:34] Priya: you can sample from production traces but obfuscate PII; if you prefer we can fuzz the patterns to match token length distribution rather than exact content.
[05:40] Michael: we need to avoid any raw PHI leaving our networks; so Redwood running synthetic runs must use obfuscated traces or synthetic generation. ok?
[05:48] Jordan: absolutely, we understand. Priya, use fuzzed traces only.
[05:52] Priya: yep will do.
[05:55] [06:00] Dana: on staging creds - currently your onboarding doc expects a service account key file. we'd prefer ephemeral tokens with short TTLs. can Redwood support ephemeral creds via STS?
[06:09] Jordan: yes, we can do STS-based ephemeral creds for the staging flow. Samir will coordinate the handshake.
[06:16] Samir: i'll send the choreography and the exact endpoints.
[06:19] [06:25] Michael: any blockers from Redwood side for us to flip gate readiness?
[06:28] Priya: blocked only by KMS decision and staging peering details. once those are in we can re-run the extended bench in 48 hours.
[06:36] Jordan: timeline check - if we get KMS and peering by Friday, SE will run the long synthetic sweep by Sunday, Samir will deliver docs Monday, and we can meet Tuesday for decision on dedicated pilot. does that align?
[06:50] Leila: yes, that works.
[06:53] [07:00] Omar: one quick question on data at rest - does Redwood persist raw request payloads by default?
[07:07] Jordan: no by default we don't persist PII; we have configurable retention and you can opt to disable payload retention entirely and just keep audit meta. we'll include that in the security pack.
[07:18] Omar: perfect.
[07:20] [07:30] Priya Shah: just to confirm, what do you need from our side this week?
[07:34] Jordan: staging VPC peering details, KMS decision, and confirm who will be on the SSO mapping call.
[07:40] Priya Shah: i'll own SSO mapping, Dana will send peering, Omar will send KMS vendor note.
[07:46] Jordan: cool. last thing — we'll attach bench traces and a short playbook for p99 troubleshooting. link will be in the follow-up.
[07:55] Michael: thanks everyone, helpful as always.
[07:58] Jordan: thanks team, we'll follow up with the security pack and bench spreadsheet. bye.

Artifacts referenced: bench spreadsheet (https://redwood.in/benchmarks/nexara-poc-5), onboarding runbook (link shared in chat), security pack (to be sent), pricing options doc (will be shared).

End transcript.
